opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jason Hansen (employee ID E044) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E044.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Jason Hansen (E044) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Payroll. Full-time employees can be granted up to write; admin requires that the employee's role owns the system, and Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Requested access exceeds the allowed level, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jason Hansen (E044) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend granting read for Payroll.
reason: Jason Hansen (E044) requested admin access to Payroll. The notes conflict on employment type: HR reports full-time Engineer (max write, since Engineer does not own Payroll), while Security reports contractor with basic security training (max read, since write requires advanced training). Admin is above the allowed level under either interpretation. Given the conflicting records, I grant the most restrictive policy-compliant level, read, which is within the maximum under both readings and is the Security agent's recommendation.

The employee is Jason Hansen (E044), requesting admin access to Payroll.

There are conflicting notes:
- HR agent says: full_time Engineer, recommendation for Payroll: write
- Security agent says: contractor with basic security training, recommendation for Payroll: read

The HR and Security agents have conflicting information about employment type. HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Requested: admin to Payroll.
Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Jason is an Engineer, so even if full-time, he can't get admin on Payroll (only up to write).

If contractor, max is read or write if advanced training (basic training → read only).

Either way, admin is above the max. So the max would be:
- If HR is right (full_time Engineer): write
- If Security is right (contractor, basic): read
